why.incidents-without-agency: An incident must be tied to an agency to enable scope aggregation, billing and hierarchical traceability.
why.incidents-without-service: Without an attached service, the incident cannot be routed to the responsible service lead nor appear in per-service reports.
why.users-without-role: A user without a role has no effective permission: they can do nothing in the app yet still take a license seat.
why.users-without-scope: An operational user with no agency or service bypasses scope filtering — they may see or create incidents out of context.
why.incidents-assigned-inactive-user: The incident is stuck: its assignee will never log in to handle it. The deadline keeps running.
why.reports-without-file: The report is flagged available but no file was persisted. Any download attempt will fail.
why.sent-notifications-without-trace: The notification is flagged sent without a timestamp or provider receipt — delivery cannot be proven.
why.invalid-recipient-notifications: Recipient format is invalid (malformed email). Any retry will fail systematically.
why.agencies-without-head: With no head, hierarchical notifications (validation, escalation) have nowhere to route.
why.services-without-head: Same as agency: no service head means no recipient for transfers/business approvals.
why.unused-incident-types: Configured type that was never picked — possibly obsolete, mis-documented, or created by mistake.

fix.incidents-without-agency: Open each incident and set its agency; also verify that creator users have an agency assigned.
fix.incidents-without-service: Set a service on the incident or a default service on its type via Settings → Incident types.
fix.users-without-role: Assign a suitable role in Users → Edit, or deactivate the account if no longer used.
fix.users-without-scope: Fill the user's agency/service; or strip their operational role if they are a global admin.
fix.incidents-assigned-inactive-user: Reassign the incident to an active user or reactivate the user in Users.
fix.reports-without-file: Check storage or file generation. A report with zero incidents is normal; an AVAILABLE report without a downloadable file is not.
fix.sent-notifications-without-trace: Identify the failing pipeline (email configuration, template, or incorrect status). Fix the cause, then let the business retry flow take over.
fix.invalid-recipient-notifications: Fix the recipient address in the user profile. Retrying is not useful until the address is valid.
fix.agencies-without-head: Set a head in Settings → Agencies.
fix.services-without-head: Set a head in Settings → Services.
fix.unused-incident-types: Check relevance; delete or disable the type in Settings → Incident types.

config.intro: Only thresholds that actually change business or security behavior are exposed here.
config.thresholdsHint: Each value below directly affects a business rule, a notification or an account protection.

thresholdGroupHints.incidents: Rules that influence overdue incidents, reminders and incident alerts.
thresholdGroupHints.reports: Duration for which generated reports remain available.
thresholdGroupHints.security: Limits that protect accounts and control email send attempts.
thresholdGroupHints.backup: Daily database backup and synchronisation to Backblaze B2.

thresholdLabels.serviceManagerSelfValidationEnabled: Validator when a manager reports an incident for their own service
thresholdLabels.validationDelayHours: Delay before a pending validation is chased (h)

thresholdDescriptions.serviceManagerSelfValidationEnabled: Applies only when the creator manages the handling service configured on the incident type. The incident then awaits validation by an administrator by default, or by the service manager if selected here. Other incidents keep their type's usual validation workflow.
thresholdDescriptions.criticalIncidentHours: How many hours a critical incident must stay open before it shows as untreated in the escalation rules. This setting sends no reminder.
thresholdDescriptions.maxTransfersBeforeAlert: Transfer count after which the incident should be monitored.
thresholdDescriptions.slaReminderIntervalHours: Minimum time between two reminders for the same overdue incident.
thresholdDescriptions.notificationMaxRetryCount: Maximum automatic attempts before considering the email durably failed.
thresholdDescriptions.loginMaxFailedAttempts: Number of failed logins before locking the account.
thresholdDescriptions.tempPasswordValidityMinutes: Validity duration of a temporary password.
thresholdDescriptions.defaultSlaHours: Delay used when the incident type has no specific deadline.
thresholdDescriptions.escalationScanIntervalMinutes: Frequency of automatic escalation rule detection.
thresholdDescriptions.maxReopenCount: Maximum number of times an incident can be reopened after being resolved or rejected.
thresholdDescriptions.reopenTimeLimitHours: Maximum allowed duration after resolution to reopen an incident.
thresholdDescriptions.autoBlockOverdueWorkingDays: Number of overdue working days (excluding Sundays) before an incident is automatically set to Blocked.
thresholdDescriptions.blockedReminderIntervalDays: Interval between two reminders for an incident that remains blocked.
thresholdDescriptions.criticalReminderIntervalHours: How often the people concerned by an open critical incident are reminded: whoever reported it, whoever is handling it, and their managers. The reminder arrives in the app and by email.
thresholdDescriptions.prolongedWaitDays: Number of continuous blocked days before automatic transition to prolonged wait.
thresholdDescriptions.validationDelayHours: How long a validation may be awaited before the expected validator is chased, administrators in copy. The treatment deadline itself only starts at validation.
thresholdDescriptions.validationReminderEnabled: Chases lingering validations at the expected validator, administrators in copy. Switching it off stops that watch without touching the rest of the workflow.
thresholdDescriptions.reportRetentionDays: Reports older than this duration are automatically deleted every day.
thresholdDescriptions.backupScheduleEnabled: Enables or disables the scheduled daily backup. Manual triggering stays available either way.
thresholdDescriptions.backupScheduleHour: Hour at which the daily backup runs. Defaults to 20:00.
thresholdDescriptions.pendingActionReminderIntervalHours: Interval between two reminders sent to whoever must resolve or close an incident, administrators in copy.
thresholdDescriptions.pendingActionInternalEnabled: In-app notification for the reminder. E-mail is set separately in the automatic e-mail catalogue, and stays off by default.

config.noChanges: No changes were made to the thresholds.
